question: Which line is our Pete's Point row, and is the North Ridge from Tenderfoot Pass a different route to add?
answer: Our stored row (mountaineering, Easy Snow) describes a snow couloir on the north face (~45 deg, 750 ft) reached via the East Fork Wallowa trail past Aneroid Lake, with an ice axe. Only one old log (snippet) mentions a north gully. The commonly reported lines are walk-ups from Tenderfoot Pass: a shorter, steeper north arm and a longer, gentler south arm (Oregon Hikers forum quoting the peak page, fetched). Tenderfoot Pass is 8,540 ft; summit 9,675 ft (forum) / 9,679.6 ft lidar (Peakbagger, most recent). Harder routes come from the west and north. So the North Ridge is distinct from the couloir and is the standard line. Pin: in the packet Peakbagger's 45.18934,-117.22031 is 0 m from the area coordinate, so I could not reproduce the 2.5 km offset; no peak-specific trailhead coordinate was fetched (Wallowa Lake Trailhead 45.26704,-117.212834 is the far start, from the Ice Lake page).
recommendation: KEEP the couloir row (retitle 'North Couloir'; grade Easy Snow fine; set season Jun-Jul since it needs snow). ADD 'North Ridge from Tenderfoot Pass' (scrambling, class 2) on or_aneroid_lake_peaks, season Jul-Sep; mention the gentler south arm in its text. Re-check the area coordinate against the summit before moving any pin.

routeRow.name: North Ridge from Tenderfoot Pass
routeRow.overview: The shorter and steeper of two walk-up arms of the summit horseshoe above Aneroid Lake. A faint path leads to a rock step near 9,500 ft with a few hands-on moves; the longer south arm is gentler.
routeRow.approach: Take the East Fork Wallowa trail from Wallowa Lake past Aneroid Lake to Tenderfoot Pass (8,540 ft), then follow the north arm of the ridge to the summit.
routeRow.descent_text: Reverse the north arm, or loop down the gentler south arm back to the pass.

evidence: https://www.oregonhikers.org/forum/viewtopic.php?p=144551 - quotes peak page: two easy walk-up arms from Tenderfoot Pass, north arm shorter/steeper; Tenderfoot Pass 8,540 ft; summit 9,675 ft
